answers.topic: How does the position of tarot cards affect a reading
answers.question: How does the position of Tarot cards affect a reading? How is it interpreted?
answers.fits: tarot card positions in a spread
answers.text:
Position gives each card its question. The same card reads differently depending on the slot it lands in.

Take the Three of Swords. In a past position it reads as grief you already went through. In a future position it warns of a hard conversation coming. In a spread position labeled obstacle, it names the heartbreak you keep replaying. The card is the same, the job is different.

The usual order: first decide what each position means before you shuffle, then read the card only through that label. A simple three-card spread is past, present, next step. A Celtic Cross has ten slots, such as what crosses you, what is beneath you and what is behind you. Reversals and the cards sitting next to each other add a second layer, so read neighbors as a sentence instead of as separate answers.

If a position confuses you, ask what that slot would sound like as a question and answer it in plain words.

answers.topic: What are some effective questions to ask during a tarot reading about career or work
answers.question: What are some effective questions to ask during a tarot card reading about career or work? How should one prepare for a career or work-related tarot card reading?
answers.text:
Ask open questions that point at your own choices, not at a verdict.

Good ones: What am I not seeing about this role? What is draining me here, and what would change that? What should I focus on in the next three months? What skill would move me forward fastest? Weak ones: Will I get the job? Will my boss fire me? Those invite a yes or no the cards cannot back up.

To prepare, spend ten minutes beforehand writing down the real situation: the offer, the deadline, what you want, what scares you. Pick one question and keep it short. Bring facts to the reading, such as salary, notice period and options, because a spread works best next to a plan you can check.

Treat what comes up as a prompt for reflection. Any career decision with money on the line still deserves numbers and advice from people who know your field.

answers.topic: Which tarot card represents a cat
answers.question: Which tarot card represents a cat?
answers.fits: tarot card that represents a cat
answers.text:
No card is officially the cat, so it depends on which trait of the cat you mean.

The Moon is the closest match for the night side: cats sit in the dark, see what you cannot and move on instinct. Several classic decks, including the Rider-Waite-Smith, do not draw a cat on it, but many modern decks do. For independence and quiet confidence, Strength fits, since it is about calm power with no force. For curiosity and restless energy, the Page of Wands or the Fool work. For a cat as a familiar or witchy companion, the High Priestess is the usual pick.

My own shorthand: Moon for the mysterious cat, Strength for the self-possessed one. Check your deck, because cat-themed decks often assign their own card, such as the Page of Wands for a playful kitten. The meaning stays with the card, and the cat is just a lens you pick.
